sentences.text: By the impugned order, the learned trial court has held that there is sufficient ground to frame charges against the revisionist accused and has proceeded to frame charge against him in the aforesaid sections.
Learned counsel for the revisionists submitted that FIR was lodged on 08.05.2013 for an alleged incident dated 27.07.2012 registered as crime no.248 of 2013 U/s 498A, 323, 504, 506 & 376 IPC.
The prosecution story is that the marriage of the elder sister of the prosecutrix was solemnized with Praveen Kumar three years ago.

On this pretext, Sudhir Kumar the real brother of Praveen Kumar made frequent visits to the house of the prosecutrix and subsequently they developed affection following which a proposal for marriage was made and was also accepted by both the families.

sentences.text: The learned counsel contended that the allegations of the FIR are absolutely false and frivolous as the revisionists always wanted to marry the prosecutrix and ultimately he also married the prosecutrix on 18.07.2013.

An application was given by opposite party no.2 to DIG Meerut region, Meerut stating therein that the prosecutrix and the revisionist are living together as husband and wife and she has no complaint whatsoever and as such she does not want to pursue the proceedings initiated by her against the revisionists.
An affidavit dated 30.01.2014 stating similar facts, was also filed before the SSP Meerut by the prosecutrix and her father.
The Investigating Officer placing reliance on the statements of the prosecutrix submitted final report on 29.03.2014.

The prosecutrix is a lady of modern values and is completely against the idea of living in a joint family and always insisted upon her husband to leave her family and started living with her separately, when the revisionist refused to agree, she very cleverly opted to misuse the proceeding initiated by her against the revisionist earlier.

In pursuance of her ill intention, the opposite party no.2 moved an application dated 09.10.2014 to the SSP Meerut seeking further investigation in the matter following which a direction was given by Circle Officer, Civil Lines, Meerut to the Inspector In-charge Civil Lines for conducting further investigation in the matter.

In pursuance of further investigation, the Investigating Officer recorded the statement of the prosecutrix on 04.01.2015, statement of other witnesses on different dates and second statement of the prosecutrix on 05.04.2015 and submitted a charge-sheet against the revisionist.
It is further contended that no offence is made out against the revisionist.
There is no medico-legal report to substantiate the allegations of assault.
Neither the revisionists nor any of his family members had demanded any dowry from the prosecutrix or her family.

The revisionist right from the inception of his marriage with the prosecutrix gave her a lot of love and affection, so that she could adjust well in her new matrimonial house but things did not go well for him due to her insistence of separate living.

Learned counsel also contended that the Apex Court in a number of cases has held that consent given by the prosecutrix to sexual intercourse with a person with whom she is deeply in love on a promise that he would marry her on a later date cannot be said to be given under a misconception of fact.
A false promise is not a fact within the meaning of the Code.
Further that there is a distinction between a false promise given on understanding by maker that it will be broken and breach of promise which is made in good faith but subsequently not fulfilled.

Where promise to marry is false and intention of maker at the time of making promise itself ws not to abide by it but to deceive woman to convince her to engage in sexual relations, there is a "misconception of fact" that vitiates woman's consent.
On the otherhand, breach of a promise cannot be said to be a false promise.
To establish a false promise, maker of promise should have had no intention of upholding his word at the time of giving it.
Learned counsel submitted that from the allegations of the FIR it is not established that the consent was on a misconception of fact.

Learned counsel placed reliance on the following case laws:
1. Sonu alias Subhash Kumar vs. State of Uttar Pradesh 2021 0 Supreme (SC) 182.
2. Maheshwar Tigga vs. State of Jharkhand 2020 0 Supreme (SC) 561.

sentences.text: Lastly it is contended that the learned court below has failed to appreciate the material and evidence on record in right perespective.

The finding of the learned court below that there is sufficient ground to frame charges against the revisionist accused is erroneous and against the evidence available on record and hence the impugned order is illegal.
The learned court below has failed to exercise its powers in a judicial manner.
No offence is made out against the revisionist, hence the impugned order is not sustainable.
Learned AGA submitted that according to allegations of the FIR, the revisionist accused under a false promise of marriage has made physical relations with prosecutrix.
When she lodged an FIR against the revisionist just to save himself from the clutches of the law, he agreed to marry with the prosecutrix.

When the matter was settled on this gesture of the revisionist and the prosecutrix moved an affidavit and gave statements in favour of the revisionist and a final report was submitted in the matter he again deceived the prosecutrix compelling her to move another application before the authorities for appropriate action.
Thereafter, the matter was further investigated and charge-sheet was submitted.
The aforesaid conduct of the revisionist itself establishes that his intention was not good, he was deceiving the prosecutrix right from the beginning.
The prosecutrix in her statement has reiterated the allegations of the FIR.
The other witnesses have also supported her.
On the basis of evidence collected during the course of investigation, charge-sheet has been submitted against the revisionist.
There is sufficient evidence on record in form of statement of prosecutrix herself and other witnesses.
The learned court below has given a thoughtful consideration and with a detailed and reasoned order has held that there is sufficient ground to frame charge.
There is no illegality in the impugned order.
The allegations of the FIR are that the revisionist has sexually exploited the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage.
He was acquainted to the prosecutrix being the younger brother of the husband of the sister of the prosecutrix and used to visit the house of prosecutrix.

At that time, he was unemployed but later on he got a job in the Railway Department and thereafter a demand of dowry was made to solemnized the marriage when it was not fulfilled then the revisionist refused to marry.
The prosecutrix and other witnesses have corroborated the allegations of the FIR.
It is settled law that at the stage of framing of charge only prima-facie case is to be seen.
At this stage mini trial cannot be conducted.
During arguments, the court enquired about the status of the trial as the charge was framed in the year 2018.
Learned counsel for the revisionist informed the court that all the witnesses of fact have been examined and some of the formal witnesses have also been examined.
Only one or two formal witnesses have remained to be examined.
As the trial is at very advance stage and near completion, it will not be appropriate at this stage to enter into the merits of the arguments submitted by learned counsel for the revisionist.

It will be just and proper to leave it to the trial court to decide all the points raised by the learned counsel for the revisionist at appropriate stage i.e. after completion of evidence at the time of final arguments/ judgment.
The revision stands disposed off accordingly.
